name: Idaho
overview: Idaho DEQ requires a Permit to Construct (PTC) before constructing or modifying sources that emit or may emit air pollutants, unless exempt. Rock crushers and certain dairies may use a Permit by Rule registration instead. General permits cover concrete batch plants, hot mix asphalt plants, and automotive coating. Tier I operating permits are Idaho's Title V permits (DEQ is the EPA-delegated agency); Tier II operating permits set facility caps, synthetic minor limits, or other limits. Rules are in IDAPA 58.01.01.

permitTypes.name: Exemptions
permitTypes.description: Self-exemption and exemption forms exist (general Exemptions Form, 6H Notification and Petition, automotive coating and cabinet making self-exemptions). One-time occurrences, such as painting a vehicle in a shop, do not require a permit.

permitTypes.name: Permit by Rule (PBR)
permitTypes.description: Registration in place of a PTC; available only to rock crushers and certain dairies.
permitTypes.citation: IDAPA 58.01.01, Sections 762-763 (dairy farms) and 795-797 (nonmetallic mineral processing plants)

permitTypes.name: General Permits
permitTypes.description: Concrete batch plants, hot-mix asphalt plants, and automotive coating operations. One-time fee of $1,500 ($1,000 application plus $500 processing) per DEQ.
permitTypes.thresholds: Per DEQ: automotive coating general permit applies to facilities using 4 gallons or less of coating materials per calendar day.

permitTypes.name: Permit to Construct (PTC)
permitTypes.description: Required before constructing or modifying sources that emit or may emit air pollutants; typically requires an air quality modeling demonstration.
permitTypes.quote: No owner or operator may commence construction or modification of any stationary source, facility, major facility, or major modification without first obtaining a permit to construct from the Department that satisfies the requirements of Sections 200 through 227 unless the source is exempted in any of Sections 220 through 223

quoteSource.name: IDAPA 58.01.01, Rules for the Control of Air Pollution in Idaho (adminrules.idaho.gov)

permitTypes.name: Tier II Operating Permit
permitTypes.description: Authorizes facility emission caps, mercury BACT limits, or synthetic minor limits; may be required for Regional Haze BART.

permitTypes.name: PSD
permitTypes.description: Section 205 covers new major facilities and major modifications in attainment or unclassifiable areas and incorporates the federal PSD requirements of 40 CFR 52.21 by reference. Applications follow Section 202 and processing follows Section 209.
permitTypes.quote: The intent of Section 205 is to incorporate the federal PSD rule requirements.

permitTypes.name: Nonattainment major NSR
permitTypes.description: Section 204 sets permit requirements for new major facilities or major modifications in nonattainment areas, as part of the Permit to Construct rules.

permitTypes.name: Tier I Operating Permit (Title V)
permitTypes.description: Consolidates applicable federal, state, and local requirements for major stationary sources into one federally enforceable permit.
permitTypes.quote: No owner or operator may operate any Tier I source without an effective Tier I operating permit.

quoteSource.name: IDAPA 58.01.01, Rules for the Control of Air Pollution in Idaho (adminrules.idaho.gov)

oilAndGas.summary: DEQ's air permitting pages list no oil-and-gas-specific air permit. Oil and gas facilities follow the PTC/Tier I/Tier II framework; federal NSPS OOOO-series and NESHAP HH apply where applicable.
